question: A copper intrauterine device (CuT 380A) can be used as emergency contraception if inserted within 5 days of unprotected intercourse, and is more than 99% effective in this indication.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually true. The copper IUD inserted within 5 days is the most effective form of emergency contraception available (>99% efficacy), compared with levonorgestrel EC (85–89%) and ulipristal acetate (98% within 72 hours).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The copper IUD is the most effective emergency contraceptive (>99% efficacy) and can be inserted up to 5 days (120 hours) after unprotected intercourse or the earliest expected date of ovulation. Its mechanism as EC is primarily spermicidal and inhibition of fertilisation.
